content: I must die. But must I die groaning? I must be imprisoned. But must I whine as well?
author: Epictetus
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. Reminding yourself of your mortality is not morbid; it is the most clarifying lens available to human consciousness. When you remember that your days are strictly numbered, petty resentments and trivial anxieties evaporate.

Epictetus understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Death gives urgency and sweetness to every ordinary afternoon. Because this day will never come again, the way you spend your attention right now is of monumental significance.
reflectionPrompt: What would happen if you met today's stress with steady acceptance rather than resistance?
